newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania eyes purchase of used U.S. fighter planes.
newsitem.headline: Romania eyes purchase of used U.S. fighter planes.

text.p: Romania's defence ministry plans to buy used fighter aircraft and transport planes from the U.S. military to bring the country's air force closer to NATO standards, a defence ministry spokesman said.

Captain Radu Enache said Defence Minister Victor Babiuc had sent a letter of intent this week to the U.S. Defence Department for the purchase of 12 F-16 or F-18 fighter jets and nine Hercules C-130 transport aircraft.
"We are not talking about new aircraft. They will come from the fleet used now by the U.S. Air Force," Enache told Reuters. He said he could not provide any figures for the planned deal.
Romania, an ex-member of the defunct Warsaw pact, has launched a diplomatic crusade to win early entry into an expanded NATO alongside favourites Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic.
It has embarked on parallel efforts to upgrade its military equipment to bring it in line with NATO standards.
Romania's 12 air-defence squadrons operate Soviet-made MiG-21s, MiG-23s and MiG-29s. Ground-attack regiments fly the Yugoslav/Romanian IAR-93 Orao.

Under a $300 million contract with the Israeli company Elbit signed last year, 25 MiG-21 fighters and 24 Puma army helicopters would be fitted with new radar and chaff/flare dispensers. The aircraft would also be upgraded to carry the latest Western weapons.
A ministry source said last month Romania also planned to buy an airborne-early-warning (AEW) aircraft, to have an AEW capability compatible with that of its potential NATO partners.

Enache also said Bell Helicopter Textron of the United States was at an advanced stage in its bid to buy a controlling stake in Romania's Intreprinderea Aeronautica Romana (IAR) helicopter to co-produce Cobra attack helicopters.
"We decided to speed up things a bit. The ministry has pledged to place a firm order for 96 Cobras," he said.

Under the plan, IAR would produce under licence 96 AH-11W Supercobra helicopters, codenamed Dracula, over 1999-2006. Four contracts with the U.S. company are expected, covering supply of materials, training of staff and technical support.
